title: Making GET Requests 🌐
ques: Write a Python script using the `requests` library to fetch data from `https://api.github.com` and print the HTTP status code.
explanation: The `requests.get()` function retrieves data from a URL, and `status_code` confirms if the request was successful (e.g., 200 OK).

title: Sending POST Data ✉️
ques: Use the `requests` library to send a POST request to `https://httpbin.org/post` with a JSON payload `{"user": "admin"}`.

answer.content:
import requests

data = {'user': 'admin'}
response = requests.post('https://httpbin.org/post', json=data)
print(response.json())

explanation: Using the `json` parameter automatically sets the `Content-Type` header to `application/json` and serializes the dictionary.

title: Adding Custom Headers 🎩
ques: Make a GET request to a URL and pass a custom `User-Agent` header to simulate a web browser request.

answer.content:
import requests

headers = {'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0'}
response = requests.get('https://httpbin.org/headers', headers=headers)
print(response.text)

explanation: Custom headers are essential for web scraping to prevent servers from blocking default automated user agents.
